quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Ride more slowly.
Read the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Wearing a quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries when riding a motorcycle. Speed does not eliminate this risk.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcyclist under normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait until it moves.
Move to another lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from it.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop now.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: within minutes of
about an hour after
about two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your ability to ride within minutes of drinking. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested.
Your skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride.
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your riding skills. Any amount of alcohol makes it unsafe to ride.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert you to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, apply both brakes together and downshift.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors show everything.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
Do not use mirrors except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs _____ attention.

options.text: Less
The same amount of
More

questions.correctAnswerText: More
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent attention than cars. Check for problems before riding, especially before highway speeds.

questions.question: During normal turns, how should the motorcycle and rider move?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should not lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays more upright to balance.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. This keeps you away from the passing driver and reduces danger for both of you.

questions.question: What color and style are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find gas, food, rest areas, and hospitals.

questions.question: At night, how can you tell if there are bumps in the road ahead when riding behind another vehicle?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: If the vehicle's taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps ahead. The vehicle ahead can also help you see the road better with its headlights.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you an escape route.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should also discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to keep control of a motorcycle during a turn?

options.text: Accelerate through the turn.
Slow down before turning.
Lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To control a turn, slow down first. Look where you want to go, lean by pressing the handlebar, and roll the throttle through the turn to steady the suspension.

questions.question: When borrowing a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Assume all controls are the same as your motorcycle.
Take it directly on the highway.
Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice with it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are on a borrowed motorcycle. Practice riding it in a safe area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding?

options.text: Yes, to keep your hands warm.
Yes, they improve grip and protect your hands.
No, gloves interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they improve grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: You may accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
You will get through the turn faster.
You will keep better control of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: When reacting to a road hazard, you should NOT:

options.text: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
Change your speed as needed.
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid telling other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you are doing by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to match the situation. Adjust your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards.
It keeps you from finding an escape route.
It gives you room to move your motorcycle safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. It also gives you room to safely move your motorcycle.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: Can be shared by the driver and passenger.
Must be on the motorcycle for both the driver and passenger.
Are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be on the motorcycle for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Good footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: A "wobble" (sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars) is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight loading.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. Most wobbles come from improper weight loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should ride in:

options.text: The left part of your lane.
The center part of your lane.
The right part of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, riding in the center of your lane is safest. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.
